title: I Used the Community-Forge Hardy Checkout on the Smith Who Hijacked My Hardy

parts.text: I stepped into anvil two at 9:06 a.m. and smith Rook was already using my numbered hardy. The board said: ONE HARDY. NINETY MINUTES. TOOLS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-six, forge steward, holding a clipboard that listed our fire. Rook shrugged. "Smiths are the anvil." I photographed the board, the booking, and his fuller in my hardy hole. Then I asked for the hardy checkout. At 9:14 the forge desk pinged why Rook's fuller sat in our hole. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The forge desk can see Rook's fuller in anvil two during our fire.

social.video_title: He hijacked my numbered hardy — Part 1/2
social.description: Community forge, a smith in my hardy hole, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the fuller. Would you have asked for the hardy checkout?

parts.text: Rook called it heat cycles until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the anvil still. The hardy went back to my numbered slot. Rook ran a slot of their own and told the next smith atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: SMITHS ARE NOT THE ANVIL. I keep our fire on a labeled hook. Rook brown-bags his fullers. The anvil finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Hardy checkout, numbered tool, and a second line on the board. Were heat cycles ever our hole?
